facts.raw_span: stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma
metastases of the liver, lungs, and peritoneum
Photodistributed erythematous to violaceous eruption
Diffuse erythema of forehead and midface, involving nasolabial folds
Erythema and edema of upper eyelids
Creatine kinase: 1088 U/L
Antinuclear antibody titer: 1:640 with speckled pattern
Jo-1 antibody: negative
MRI showed mild short TI inversion recovery hyperintensity of bilateral vastus lateralis and rectus femoris muscles
Vastus lateralis muscle biopsy showed atrophy of type II muscle fibers
Grade 4/5 strength on resisted abduction of shoulders bilaterally
Limited flexion of both hips

concepts.why: Patient presents with skin symptoms and muscle weakness, elevated creatine kinase, and muscle biopsy showing atrophy of type II muscle fibers, which are characteristic of dermatomyositis.
Patient has a history of malignant melanoma and presents with dermatomyositis-like symptoms, suggesting a paraneoplastic syndrome.
Patient has elevated creatine kinase, antinuclear antibody positivity, and muscle biopsy showing atrophy of type II muscle fibers, which are characteristic of autoimmune myopathy.
Patient has antinuclear antibody positivity and a speckled pattern, which can be seen in lupus-like syndromes.
Patient has muscle weakness, elevated creatine kinase, and muscle biopsy showing atrophy of type II muscle fibers, which are characteristic of polymyositis.
Patient has a history of malignant melanoma and presents with dermatomyositis-like symptoms, suggesting a melanoma-associated paraneoplastic syndrome.
Patient has elevated creatine kinase, antinuclear antibody positivity, and muscle biopsy showing atrophy of type II muscle fibers, which are characteristic of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy.
Patient has a history of malignant melanoma and presents with unexplained systemic symptoms, suggesting a paraneoplastic syndrome.

rationales.F01: The presence of stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma suggests a possible paraneoplastic syndrome, which increases the likelihood of C02 and C06.
rationales.F06: Elevated creatine kinase levels are a strong indicator of muscle damage, which is consistent with dermatomyositis and polymyositis.
rationales.F08: The absence of Jo-1 antibodies makes polymyositis less likely, but does not rule it out entirely.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma and metastases, combined with the specific skin symptoms such as photodistributed erythematous to violaceous eruption, support the diagnosis of Melanoma-associated dermatomyositis, which is a subtype of dermatomyositis that is directly linked to melanoma.
